decisions.decision: Type carries node category (ELEMENT/TEXT/TEXT_REF), never the tag name
decisions.rationale: Keeps the TLV registry tiny while the XML vocabulary stays open; identity moves into the value as an interned name

decisions.decision: Two-pass encode: measure into a cache, then emit from it
decisions.rationale: TLV puts Length before Value; buffering the value would cost O(payload). Peak memory becomes O(depth) plus one long per node

decisions.decision: Name and value ids assigned pre-order, before descending, and never written to the wire
decisions.rationale: Both sides derive the same ids from document order; putting ids on the wire would cost bytes and add a desync mode

decisions.decision: Both passes build tables from empty; emit pass gets fresh tables
decisions.rationale: Carrying pass 1's populated table into pass 2 makes every measured length too large and produces a silently truncated document

decisions.decision: TEXT_REF as a separate type code rather than a ValueRef field inside TEXT
decisions.rationale: Saving becomes (k-1)(L-1) instead of L(k-1)-k, so values that never repeat cost exactly what they did before interning existed
(k-1)(L-1) is zero at L=1 and negative at L=0, where a 2-byte empty literal would become a 3-byte reference

decisions.decision: The intern threshold lives only in the encoder; the decoder registers every literal
decisions.rationale: Ids stay in step without the decoder knowing the rule, so tuning the threshold is not a format change

decisions.decision: No cryptographic hash, and no digest on the wire
decisions.rationale: Dictionary<string,_> resolves collisions by comparing strings. A SHA-256 reference would be ~34 bytes framed, breaking even only above ~33, against 3 for an ordinal
Matches CBOR's split between stringref (tag 25) and sharable (tags 28/29). Identity preservation, if ever needed, requires a separate type code keyed on reference equality

decisions.decision: Instance sharing is a decoder option, defaulting to share
decisions.rationale: The format says nothing about identity. Sharing is free and unobservable for immutable strings, and correct for RPC
User works alone; PR-based enforcement was removed and replaced with local hooks plus force-push/deletion protection

context_notes: Conversational design-then-build loop: settle a format question in discussion, write it into docs/, implement against the doc, benchmark, and record findings back into docs/tlv-performance.md. Every change goes through a git-flow feature branch because the repo's own pre-commit hook blocks direct commits on main and develop. Verification standard in this project is high: claims get checked against reality (independent re-implementation of the hex vector, mutation testing of the encoder, freshness checks on benchmark artifacts) rather than asserted.
